evidence.excerpt:
Long-term memory remains a fundamental bottleneck for large language model
(LLM) agents across sessions. Existing systems typically adopt a write-then-
retrieve paradigm, storing context-dependent dialogue fragments and retrieving
them via nearest-neighbor search in continuous embedding space. This design
yields unstable access units and systematically misses logically related but lexi-
cally distant evidence. We propose MemCode, a long-term agent memory frame-
work that couples retrieval-oriented writing with discrete associative retrieval.
MemCode rewrites dialogue into self-contained atomic memory units (AMUs),
maps AMUs into a learnable codebook with isomorphic semantic quantization
(ISQ), and uses codebook co-occurrence topology as a retrieval path comple-
mentary to vector search. For long-term memory stores, MemCode separates on-
line atomic writes from asynchronous offline

evidence.excerpt:
MemCode, a unified write–index–
retrieve–consolidate framework that addresses the write–retrieve mismatch in long-term agent mem-
ory by organizing memory around atomic facts and discrete representations. (2) We introduce AMUs
as the retrieval unit of this framework, turning raw dialogue into self-contained and source-grounded
facts. (3) We pair AMUs with ISQ and codebook topology, giving each fact both a continuous vector
interface and a discrete associative path for evidence beyond local embedding neighborhoods. (4)
On LongMemEval-S, MemCode reaches 78.40%/74.60% Overall with GPT-4o-mini/Qwen3 after
asynchronous consolidation; on LoCoMo it reaches 79.55%/76.88%, while keeping construction
runtime roughly 3∼21×faster than LightMem and over an order of magnitude faster than A-MEM
and MemoryOS.

Online atomic writes can accumulate duplicate facts, outdated states, and retrieval interference.
MemCode handles this with an asynchronous consolidation engine outside the online path. It back-
fills dense vectors, filters invalid entries, and applies hierarchical agglomerative clustering (HAC)
based on cosine distance [31]:
G= HAC

F;d(u i, uj) = 1− vi ·v j∥vi∥∥vj∥ , dmax = 1−τ  .(12)
Here,v i is the dense vector of AMUu i produced by the same encoder used by Path A,τis the con-
figured minimum cosine similarity for grouping, andGis the candidate cluster set. Large clusters
are split by time. Before entering the LLM, a gate skips count-sensitive clusters, restricts update-
sensitive clusters, and avoids cross-speaker mixing. Passing clusters are assigned to AGGREGATE,
MERGE, or UPDATE, with fewer new facts than archived facts. After write-back, Pointer Forward-
ing marks old facts

evidence.excerpt:
A Limitations
MemCode targets retrieval-intensive long-term conversational memory, not fully deployed agents
with planning, tool use, and interactive adaptation. Its LLM-based AMU writing can miss or distort
implicit motivations, emotions, and pragmatic cues; these cases explain why full-context methods
remain competitive on LoCoMo Open and bound our claims to structured memory retrieval. Our
HippoRAG2 comparison also measures one-shot graph construction over complete LoCoMo histo-
ries; repeated graph maintenance in a growing online memory is outside the present evaluation.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: The codebook is trained offline on DailyDialog and frozen before benchmark evaluation, while headline accuracy is measured on LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S against ground-truth references using a fixed LLM judge, with repeated-run stability and paired trace analyses reported.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Benchmark QA accuracy on LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S, judged by GPT-4o-mini against reference answers, plus construction runtime, token, and call measurements.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: Offline VQ codebook training on DailyDialog via predictive context-response generation and commitment losses, plus prompt-instructed LLM atomic memory writing.

primary.claim_evidence_alignment: Reported gains in QA accuracy and construction speed align with empirical results in Tables 1-4, supported by sensible category-level trade-offs (e.g., slight loss in fine temporal precision after consolidation, lower open-domain extraction fidelity).
primary.evaluation_assessment: Evaluation across LongMemEval-S and LoCoMo benchmarks includes multiple backbones (GPT-4o-mini and Qwen3-30B), comparison against multiple memory baselines (LightMem, A-MEM, Mem0, MemoryOS, LangMem, HippoRAG2), explicit fixed-budget retrieval controls (BM25, HyDE), and repeated-run stability checks.

evaluation_independence.corroboration_summary: System performance is corroborated by frozen ground-truth question-answering benchmarks (LoCoMo, LongMemEval-S) evaluated via structured LLM matching against reference answers, objective runtime measurements, and paired human/error trace inspections.
evaluation_independence.final_evaluation_signal: Benchmark QA accuracy judged by GPT-4o-mini against ground-truth references on LoCoMo and LongMemEval-S, alongside system construction runtime and token counts.
evaluation_independence.optimization_signal: The VQ codebook is trained offline on DailyDialog via predictive context-response generation and commitment losses, while online writing uses prompt-instructed LLM abstraction.

primary.limitations: The authors clearly delineate boundaries: AMU extraction struggles with implicit motivation/affect compared to full-context methods, HippoRAG2 comparison was static rather than dynamic online maintenance, and performance varies with backbone generation verbosity.
primary.method_assessment: The methodology is thoroughly detailed, describing dialogue atomization with read-only background, isomorphic semantic quantization using a DailyDialog-pretrained T5 codebook, transition scoring over code co-occurrence topology, and asynchronous hierarchical clustering consolidation.
primary.quality_rationale: The work presents a clear, well-supported technical contribution to agentic memory architecture. Extensive ablations rule out trivial candidate budget increases, and codebook behavior is analyzed extensively without circular optimization.
primary.scoped_contribution: MemCode is an agent memory framework combining atomic memory unit abstraction, discrete semantic quantization via a trained VQ codebook, dual-path (vector and codebook topology) retrieval, and asynchronous consolidation to improve long-term memory QA accuracy and construction efficiency.

scholarly_quality.rationale: The work presents a clear, well-supported technical contribution to agentic memory architecture. Extensive ablations rule out trivial candidate budget increases, and codebook behavior is analyzed extensively without circular optimization.
scholarly_quality.uncertainty: The authors clearly delineate boundaries: AMU extraction struggles with implicit motivation/affect compared to full-context methods, HippoRAG2 comparison was static rather than dynamic online maintenance, and performance varies with backbone generation verbosity.
